title: Occupational Health Legislation: Factories Act, ESI, and Workers Benefits

steps.title: What the Factories Act 1948 covers
steps.tx: Parliament enacted the **Factories Act 1948** to regulate health, safety, welfare, and working hours inside factories, with the last major amendment in 1987. A factory means premises where a manufacturing process runs with power and ten or more workers, or without power and twenty or more workers. State governments appoint the Chief Inspector of Factories and certifying surgeons who enforce the Act.
steps.say: The Factories Act of 1948 is the basic safety law for Indian factories. It applies where ten workers use power, or twenty work without power.

Maximum 48 hours a week, weekly holiday, overtime at double wages

steps.tx: The **Factories Act 1948** regulates health, safety, welfare, and working hours, with a major amendment in 1987. A factory is premises running a manufacturing process with ten or more workers if power is used, or twenty or more if power is not used. State governments appoint the Chief Inspector of Factories and certifying surgeons to enforce the Act. Machine guarding and fencing are among the safety conditions those inspectors are on the floor to verify.
steps.say: The Factories Act of 1948, amended in 1987, covers premises with ten workers on power or twenty without it. Chief inspectors and certifying surgeons enforce health, safety, hours, and welfare, including guards on machines.

steps.title: Health provisions inside the factory
steps.tx: Under the **health provisions of the Factories Act**, the occupier must keep floors clean, dispose of effluents safely, maintain temperature and humidity within comfort limits, and prevent overcrowding. A room is overcrowded when each worker has less than the prescribed cubic space. Artificial humidification must use purified water, and spittoons, dustbins, and first aid boxes are compulsory in larger units.
steps.say: Inside the factory, the Act fixes cleanliness, ventilation, and space per worker. It also requires first aid boxes and safe disposal of dust and fumes.

left.title: Employer must provide
points: Safe drinking water points away from urinals
Ventilation that removes dust and fumes at source
Lighting that avoids glare and eye strain
One first aid box for every 150 workers

right.title: Worker must observe
points: Use guards and protective equipment provided
Report defective machinery to the manager

steps.title: Hours, leave, and young workers
steps.tx: The Act caps adult work at nine hours a day and forty eight hours a week, with a rest interval after five hours of continuous work, which together define **regulated factory working hours**. Women cannot work between seven in the evening and six in the morning. Children below fourteen years are banned, adolescents of fifteen to eighteen need a certificate of fitness, and every worker earns one day of leave for twenty days worked.
steps.say: An adult may work at most nine hours a day and forty eight hours a week. Night work for women and factory work for young children are prohibited.

nodes.label: Maximum 9 hours work in one day

steps.title: Notifiable occupational diseases
steps.tx: Schedule III of the Act lists **notifiable industrial diseases** such as lead poisoning, asbestosis, silicosis, occupational dermatitis, and noise induced hearing loss, which the manager and the attending doctor must report to the Chief Inspector. Certifying surgeons examine young workers, inspect dangerous processes, and investigate suspected occupational disease. Failure to notify is a punishable offence under the Act.
steps.say: Certain dust and chemical diseases must be reported to the factory inspector. Silicosis, lead poisoning, and asbestosis are classic notifiable diseases in India.

rows: Lead poisoning with anaemia and wrist drop

steps.title: The ESI Act and social security
steps.tx: The **Employees State Insurance Act 1948** introduced contributory social insurance for workers in factories and establishments, financed by employer and employee contributions to the ESI Corporation. It covers medical care and cash benefits during sickness, maternity, disablement, and death due to employment injury. Medical care extends to the worker's family through ESI dispensaries and hospitals.
steps.say: The ESI Act pools contributions from workers and employers. In return, the worker gets free medical care and cash support during sickness or injury.

steps.title: Cash benefits under ESI
steps.tx: Six cash and medical benefits flow from the scheme, and the **sickness benefit under ESI** pays about seventy percent of wages for up to ninety one days in two benefit periods. Extended sickness benefit continues for listed long term diseases, while enhanced sickness benefit pays full wages for sterilisation. Maternity benefit now runs up to twenty six weeks for women with the required contribution record.
steps.say: Sickness benefit replaces about seventy percent of wages for up to ninety one days. Maternity benefit under ESI now extends to twenty six weeks.

rows: About 70 percent wages, up to 91 days
Pension graded by loss of earning capacity
Family pension after fatal employment injury

steps.tx: Six cash and medical benefits come from the scheme, and the **sickness benefit under ESI** pays about seventy percent of wages for up to ninety one days across two benefit periods. Extended sickness benefit continues for listed long term diseases. Enhanced sickness benefit pays full wages for sterilisation. Maternity benefit for a woman with the required contributions now lasts up to twenty six weeks. The dispensary is where the medical side of those cash rules is delivered.
steps.say: Sickness benefit replaces about seventy percent of wages for as long as ninety one days. Long illnesses can extend it, sterilisation is paid at full wages, and maternity benefit reaches twenty six weeks.

steps.title: Disablement and dependants benefits
steps.tx: When an employment injury causes permanent loss of earning capacity, the insured person receives **disablement benefit under ESI** as a lifelong pension proportionate to that loss, assessed by a medical board. If the injury proves fatal, dependants receive a monthly family pension shared among the widow, children, and dependent parents. Temporary disablement pays about ninety percent of wages until recovery.
steps.say: A permanently disabled worker gets a lifelong pension based on lost earning capacity. If he dies, his family receives the dependants benefit pension.

left.title: Temporary disablement
points: Stops when the worker resumes duty

steps.title: Ergonomics and fitness examinations
steps.tx: Fitting the job to the worker rather than forcing the worker to the job is the science of **ergonomics in occupational health**, which redesigns tools, posture, and workload to prevent fatigue and musculoskeletal injury. The pre placement examination at recruitment places each worker in a job suited to his physical capacity, while periodic medical examinations detect early dust, noise, or chemical damage in exposed groups.
steps.say: Ergonomics redesigns the workstation so the body is not strained. A medical examination before placement keeps an unfit worker away from a harmful job.

rows: At recruitment, matches worker fitness to job demands
At fixed intervals for workers in hazardous processes
After suspected poisoning or a notifiable disease report
After long sickness absence or major injury

steps.title: Sickness absenteeism and safety codes
steps.tx: Days lost when a worker stays away certified sick are measured as **sickness absenteeism in industry**, a sensitive index of both worker health and factory morale. Causes span genuine illness, occupational injury, poor sanitation, and social factors such as alcohol use and long commutes. The four Occupational Safety and Health codes now subsume the Factories Act and related laws into a single modern framework.
steps.say: Sickness absenteeism counts certified sick days lost per worker each year. Rising rates point to poor health, poor sanitation, or poor morale in the plant.
